data.headline: Long Treasury yields rise as bond futures positions diverge
data.summary: The thirty-year Treasury yield rose to 5.26% on November 6, up from 5.25% on November 5. In the earlier November 3 Treasury bond futures report, both the asset-manager net long and the leveraged-fund net short increased.

bull.text: The asset-manager net long in Treasury bond futures rose from 383,981 to 415,379 contracts between October 27 and November 3.

bear.text: The thirty-year yield rose 1 basis point while the ten-year rose 2 basis points to 4.86%. Rising long-term yields generally reduce the value of existing fixed-rate bonds, with greater sensitivity at longer duration.

watch.text: The Treasury bond futures leveraged-fund net short grew from 150,393 to 166,257 contracts. Over the later Treasury observation dates the thirty-year minus ten-year yield spread narrowed from 41 to 40 basis points.

limitations: The Treasury yields are dated November 6. This report has no verified ETF closing-price or return observation.
The CFTC observations are weekly futures positions as of November 3. ETF flows and investor intent require separate evidence.
